As the weather cools down, we start spending more time indoors. The kitchen becomes the gathering spot again, the living room starts getting more use than the backyard, and suddenly, all the little things that bothered you about your home during the summer are really hard to ignore.

Maybe you cooked on the grill all summer, but now that you’re spending more time inside, the lack of counter space is becoming harder to ignore. Maybe you’re running out of room to store everyday essentials, or your layout makes it difficult to host family and friends comfortably.

Trying to decide whether to remodel your home or move? Before you start browsing real estate listings or planning a renovation, there are three questions you should ask yourself.
1️⃣ Do you love your location?
If you love your neighborhood, have great schools nearby, or can’t imagine leaving the community you’ve built, it may be worth exploring how your current home could better meet your needs before deciding to move.
2️⃣ Can your home structurally support what you need?
Maybe you’re dreaming of a larger kitchen, more functional storage, an additional bathroom, or more room for your family. It’s time to consider whether your existing home can accommodate those changes and what it would take to make them happen.
3️⃣ Would the cost of moving get you the remodel you want?
Buying a new home comes with more expenses than the purchase price alone. Between moving costs, closing costs, potentially higher monthly payments, and the expense of making a new house feel like home, it’s worth comparing the full cost of relocating with what you could accomplish by investing in your current home.
Of course, there’s no one-size-fits-all answer. The best choice depends on your home, your priorities, your family, and what makes the most sense for your future.

Thinking about selling your home? Before you remodel, it’s worth asking: which improvements will actually matter to a future buyer?
Not every renovation is going to give you the same return, and spending more doesn’t necessarily mean getting more back when it’s time to sell.
Kitchens and bathrooms are often high-impact spaces because buyers notice when they feel dated or don’t function well. Improving curb appeal can also make a difference before a buyer even walks through the front door. But that doesn’t mean you need to completely transform these spaces. Smaller, targeted updates can sometimes make more sense than a full, high-end renovation when your goal is to improve the home before selling.
On the other hand, highly personalized upgrades or major renovations that go far beyond what’s typical for the neighborhood may not recoup their full cost at resale. If an improvement is designed around very specific tastes or adds features that future buyers may not value in the same way, you may not see that investment reflected in the sale price.
The key is knowing what makes sense for your home, your market, and your timeline before you start making decisions.
That’s one of the conversations we’ll be having at our upcoming seminar, Remodel or Relocate? Insights From Real Estate & Design Pros.

Nothing makes us happier than hearing a homeowner say they love their new space. That`s why we do what we do.
With this project, our goal was to transform these rooms into spaces the homeowners could love for years to come: making them feel more open and functional while still honoring the character of the original 1980s home.
The original kitchen felt cramped and dated, so we looked beyond the kitchen itself to find a solution. By borrowing square footage from the dining room and pushing back the refrigerator wall, we created room for a large island and a much more comfortable flow for cooking, gathering, and entertaining.
The original dining room took on a completely new purpose as a home office. We added french doors that bring in natural light. We love using French doors because they help to create some privacy in a space while still allowing for connection to the rest of the home. We also added custom wainscoting that preserves the character of the original space. Matching the existing trim required carefully rebuilding the wall, but that attention to detail meant the new work felt like it had always belonged there.
The home now feels completely different, but it still feels like itself.
That balance is one of our favorite parts of remodeling: finding thoughtful ways to make a home work better for the people who live there without losing the details that make it special.

Thinking about selling your home? Before you remodel, it’s worth asking: which improvements will actually matter to a future buyer?

Not every renovation is going to give you the same return, and spending more doesn’t necessarily mean getting more back when it’s time to sell.

Kitchens and bathrooms are often high-impact spaces because buyers notice when they feel dated or don’t function well. Improving curb appeal can also make a difference before a buyer even walks through the front door. But that doesn’t mean you need to completely transform these spaces. Smaller, targeted updates can sometimes make more sense than a full, high-end renovation when your goal is to improve the home before selling.

On the other hand, highly personalized upgrades or major renovations that go far beyond what’s typical for the neighborhood may not recoup their full cost at resale. If an improvement is designed around very specific tastes or adds features that future buyers may not value in the same way, you may not see that investment reflected in the sale price.

The key is knowing what makes sense for your home, your market, and your timeline before you start making decisions.

We love using French doors because they help to create some privacy in a space while still allowing for connection to the rest of the home. We also added custom wainscoting that preserves the character of the original space. Matching the existing trim required carefully rebuilding the wall, but that attention to detail meant the new work felt like it had always belonged there.

The home now feels completely different, but it still feels like itself.

That balance is one of our favorite parts of remodeling: finding thoughtful ways to make a home work better for the people who live there without losing the details that make it special.

When you’re investing in your home, you shouldn’t have to wonder what was missed, if anything might go wrong, or whether something will need to be redone down the road. That should all be taken care of for you. 

That’s why we put so much thought into what happens before construction even begins. Our designers and our production team work together from the start to think through the details, coordinate the moving pieces, select materials that are made to stand up to everyday life, and anticipate potential challenges before they become problems.

Because yes, quality can be about how beautiful the finished space looks, but it’s also about how the space stands to the wear of time. You shouldn’t have to worry about it after the construction is complete.

We make sure the cabinet opens exactly the way it should or the electric rerouting is planned correctly so you don’t have to hire someone a year later to fix it. We use materials that can handle years of daily use so the final product lasts as long as you want it to. We consider the details and think ahead so they never become an issue.

When you work with an experienced design-build team, you’re investing in the promise of quality craftsmanship, as well as the planning and expertise that help make sure it’s built to last.

Curious what remodel features people have been asking about lately? Here’s one: full panel refrigerators.

If you’re someone who wants their kitchen to feel clean, custom, and elevated, this is a great choice. Unlike a standard stainless steel refrigerator, a panel-ready model blends right into your cabinetry, creating a seamless look with fewer visual interruptions.

It’s not just about looks either. You still get the performance and functionality you expect from a high-quality refrigerator, but with a finish that feels intentionally integrated into the design of the kitchen.

We especially love full panel refrigerators in open-concept kitchens, where the refrigerator can otherwise become a major visual focal point. Since this version of the appliance has cabinetry panels across the front, it seamlessly blends into the room, making the entire space feel more cohesive and coordinated.

It’s a design choice that can make a kitchen feel custom and luxurious without calling too much attention to itself. A decision you’ll never regret.

Curious if a full panel refrigerator makes sense for your kitchen? Book a complimentary consultation with our design team or stop by the showroom. We’d love to help you choose the features you’ll be obsessed with for years to come!

When you have a smaller kitchen, it’s easy to assume there just isn’t enough room to create the space you want. We’ve had this conversation with a lot of people, so you’re not alone. But here’s the thing we tell everyone: square footage doesn’t tell the whole story.

The right design choices can make a smaller footprint feel open and functional while still giving you plenty of personality. It’s about being intentional with every inch, deciding what you actually need and figuring out what your kitchen actually needs to work well for you.

That might mean skipping upper cabinets to keep the room open. It could mean using shelving for the things you reach for most, incorporating custom cabinetry to maximize storage, or choosing a few standout details that give the kitchen personality without overwhelming the space.

This kitchen in a historic Providence home is a great example of how those choices can work together. The inset cabinetry gives the kitchen a clean, streamlined look without making the cabinetry feel visually heavy. Open shelves provide accessible storage while keeping the walls feeling lighter than a full set of upper cabinets. The overhang on the countertop creates room for bar stools so they can be pushed underneath the counter when they aren’t in use. That way, they don’t have to take up valuable floor space all the time.

We want homeowners with smaller kitchens to remember that you don’t need a huge footprint to create a kitchen that feels custom, functional, and completely your own.

If you’ve been writing off your kitchen because you think it’s too small to remodel, let’s take another look at what might be possible. Schedule a complimentary consultation through the link in our bio!

Before you start planning an addition, ask yourself one question: are you using all the space you already have?

If you have an unfinished basement, you may already have the square footage you need. Finishing it can be a practical way to add meaningful living space without expanding the footprint of your home.

And now you get to design that space around what your family actually needs without the hassle of laying new foundation. A basement could become a home office, a playroom, a guest space or in-law apartment, a workout area, or even a combination of spaces that can adapt as your needs change. With thoughtful planning, an unfinished basement can go from overlooked square footage to one of the most useful parts of your home.

With that said, finishing a basement comes with its own considerations. You need to think about layout, lighting, flooring, storage, egress, HVAC, and how the space will connect to the rest of your home. That’s why having an experienced team involved from the beginning can make such a difference.

What if your basement truly felt like another part of your home instead of the dark space downstairs?

That was the goal with this transformation. As with many basements, the space had been through a lot over the years, including water and fire damage. This project was really about creating a completely fresh start for the space.

With that in mind, we got to work. Now, it’s almost unrecognizable. Warm-toned flooring carries throughout the basement, while shades of blue add personality throughout the space. We added blue cabinetry in the bathroom that picks up on the subtle blue veining in the sink countertop, as well as a softer tile flooring that helps bring texture into the bathroom.

The homeowner wanted a dedicated space for their gym equipment, so now there’s an area in the basement that’s built specifically for that purpose. We also created a new laundry room and additional closets, one of which we tucked beneath the stairs, creating some unique hidden storage. We’re always looking for areas that could easily be overlooked to turn into unique spaces the homeowners can actually use.

Thoughtful design can completely change the way you experience a space, and that includes a basement! With the right planning, it can feel connected to the rest of your home while giving your family even more space to live, work, and enjoy.

When you feel like your home is running out of space, it’s easy to assume the only solution is to build more of it. But before you start thinking about adding square footage, take a look at the spaces you already have.

We’re often quick to write off the spaces that aren’t working for us. The basement becomes the place where everything gets stored. The extra room sits mostly empty. The entryway becomes a pile of shoes, bags, and everything else that doesn’t have a home. But those spaces aren’t necessarily the problem. 

The potential is there. Sometimes it just takes a different way of looking at the space.

This basement is a great example. What started as a dark, overlooked space became a collection of purposeful rooms, including a gym, laundry room, and bathroom. Instead of adding onto the home, the design found new ways for the existing space to work better for the homeowners.

That’s often the first step in transforming an underused space: figuring out what you actually need and then creating a plan to make the space work for you.

That’s where a multi-room remodel can get complicated.

You’re not just planning individual spaces. You’re thinking about how they connect, how the design flows from one room to the next, and how all of the pieces work together. There are also the things you may not see in the finished space, like structural changes, plumbing rough-ins, electrical updates, egress requirements, or HVAC extensions.

Every decision can affect something else.

That’s why experience matters so much when you’re remodeling multiple spaces. An experienced design-build team can look at the entire project from the beginning, considering the design, construction, systems, and how your family will actually use each space. A well-designed mudroom can change how your whole house feels.

When you have a busy household, the chaos has to go somewhere. And usually, that looks like backpacks landing by the stairs, shoes piling up by the door, jackets ending up on the nearest chair, and somehow, the dog’s leash never being where you thought you left it.

A functional mudroom gives all of those everyday things a place to go.

Think designated zones for each family member. That might mean a drop zone where backpacks and bags can be unloaded as soon as you walk through the door or hooks placed at heights that are reachable for every member of the family. Add a bench with storage underneath for shoes or a dedicated spot for those little things you’re constantly reaching for, like dog treats, and suddenly the room is doing a lot more than storing stuff.

When everything has a designated place, fewer things make their way into the rest of the house. The mudroom functions as a way to contain the chaos of family life. The entryway stays clearer, the kitchen counter stays less cluttered, the dog’s leash is always in the same place, and getting out the door becomes just a little easier.

Maybe it’s the extra bedroom you don’t really need, or the awkward bonus room, or the space that somehow became a dumping ground for everything without a designated home. Even though you have no idea what to do with them right now, these are all underutilized spaces that are brimming with potential.

All that room needs is a little imagination and some intentional thinking.

Take this space for example. It had the potential to be a lot of things, but when the clients spoke about their lifestyle, it made sense to dedicate the space as a home office. Since both parties needed space to work, his-and-hers workstations made sense to create dedicated spaces to focus, while the generous layout keeps the room feeling open and comfortable.

Why should laundry always live in the basement?

If most of your laundry happens upstairs, carrying baskets up and down the stairs can become one of those everyday inconveniences you simply learn to live with. But you don’t necessarily need a huge laundry room to make that routine easier.

A smaller laundry area tucked onto the second floor can put everything right where you need it. A compact washer and dryer can fit into a surprisingly small footprint, and thoughtful additions like a sink for stain treatment or dedicated storage can make the space even more functional.

This kind of setup isn’t just useful for a second-floor laundry area either. A compact laundry unit can be a smart solution for in-law suites or accessory dwelling units, where space is often limited but having everyday conveniences close at hand can make a big difference. Instead of dedicating an entire room to laundry, you can create a functional setup that fits neatly into the space you have while still giving you the independence and convenience of having laundry right where you need it.

When you think about the return on investment of a remodel, you probably think about resale value.

And yes, that’s certainly part of it; a thoughtfully designed kitchen or bathroom can add value to your home. But we’d actually argue that the return you’re getting every day is just as important.

Maybe it’s the 10 minutes you get back every morning because your bathroom finally works for your routine. Or maybe it’s not having to dig through three cabinets to find the coffee maker, filters, and coffee beans. Or being able to cook dinner without bumping into everyone else in the kitchen and then sitting down in a space that cultivates conversation. It could even be something as simple as walking into a room that feels calm instead of cluttered.

Those moments don’t have a dollar amount attached to them, but they all have value. Think about how much time a functional layout saves. Thoughtful storage reduces frustration and a space designed around the way you actually live makes everyday life a little easier. 

We’d also be remiss if we didn’t bring up the joy of finally having a home that feels like it’s yours. A remodel allows you to customize the space to be suited to your needs: A kitchen where everyone naturally gathers or a bathroom that feels like a retreat.

Investing in your home doesn’t have to be about maximizing what you’ll get back when you sell. You deserve to enjoy the investment while you live there, too.

If you’ve been hesitating because you’re not sure whether a remodel is “worth it,” maybe the better question is: what would it be worth to you to stop working around your home and start having it work for you? Our Process
We’re obsessed with every detail in our four-step Design/Build process. Our team of experts will manage every aspect of your project from idea to completion to ensure your remodel exceeds your expectations.
Imagine
We start with questions. Why? Because we want to truly understand your lifestyle and how you’ll use your new space. Then, we’ll visit your home to measure and discuss ideas with your budget in mind.
Conceptualize
Gain a true picture of the possibilities! Next, we’ll meet in our Design Center to present design concepts with our 3D modeling software to see how your new space could look and feel. We’ll review the scope of work and adjust based upon your needs. Our Project Development Agreement outlines selected concepts and budget, so you can move forward with detailed design and product selections.
Collaborate
With your feedback, we’ll transform your concepts into detailed plans and guide you through the myriad of product choices to prepare the roadmap for your new space. We’ll be by your side as you select everything from cabinetry, countertops, to plumbing fixtures, flooring, lighting, accessories and more. About Us
As a family-owned, full-service Design Build residential remodeler, we are renowned for our nationally award-winning work in kitchens, baths, mudrooms, pantries, built-ins, multi-room renovations, game rooms, bar areas, and more.
We specialize in creating spaces that cater to various life stages, from raising families and entertaining friends to providing for loved ones or facilitating aging in place. Where other companies only offer limited services, we take a complete approach to every job, overseeing the planning, designing, and installation of every project. This gives us better control over scheduling, quality and costs, and results in a project that is completed with fewer delays and – a very important consideration – less stress for our customers!

From the very beginning, we have an emphasis on hiring talented people with a passion for remodeling and designing, and a desire to please customers. Our passion for professionalism and commitment to customer satisfaction has led the company to be the leading design/build company in the area.
An Unparalleled Guarantee

This is on top of the manufacturer warranties that accompany many of the products we install. No remodeling company can deliver the peace of mind that comes with such a strong guarantee.

About RIKB Design Build
What is RIKB Design Build?
RIKB Design Build is an award-winning residential design-build remodeling company serving homeowners throughout Rhode Island, southeastern Massachusetts, and eastern Connecticut. Since 1989, we’ve specialized in kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, home additions, basement finishing, and whole-home renovations. Our integrated design-build process brings design, project management, and construction together under one experienced team.
What is a design-build remodeling company?
A design-build company manages every phase of a remodeling project, from design and material selection to construction and project management. Instead of hiring separate designers, architects, and contractors, homeowners work with a single coordinated team throughout the project.
What types of remodeling projects does RIKB Design Build specialize in?
RIKB Design Build specializes in custom residential remodeling, including kitchen and bathroom remodels, whole-home renovations, basement finishing, home additions, mudrooms, laundry rooms, home offices, built-ins, and aging-in-place renovations. Whether you’re updating a single room or transforming your entire home, our design-build team creates beautiful, functional spaces tailored to your lifestyle and goals.
What areas does RIKB Design Build serve for home remodeling?
RIKB Design Build proudly serves homeowners throughout Rhode Island, southeastern Massachusetts, and eastern Connecticut from our Warwick, Rhode Island, Design Center. If you’re planning a kitchen remodel, bathroom renovation, home addition, or whole-home remodel, our team can help determine whether your project falls within our service area.
Why should I choose RIKB Design Build for my remodeling project?
For nearly four decades, RIKB Design Build has helped homeowners throughout Rhode Island create beautiful, functional spaces tailored to their lifestyles. Our collaborative design-build process, experienced team, exceptional craftsmanship, and commitment to customer satisfaction deliver a full-service remodeling experience that is organized, transparent, and enjoyable from the first design meeting through the final walkthrough.
How do I get started with RIKB Design Build?
Getting started is easy. Schedule a consultation with our design team to discuss your goals, lifestyle, investment range, and vision for your home. We’ll answer your questions, explain our design-build process, and help you determine the best path forward for your remodeling project.
Can I visit your Design Center before starting my remodeling project?
Absolutely! We encourage it. Whether you’re just gathering ideas or ready to start planning, visiting our 3,000+ square-foot Design Center in Warwick, Rhode Island, is a great first step toward bringing your vision to life. Explore inspiring displays of kitchens, bathrooms, and living spaces while comparing cabinetry, countertops, tile, flooring, lighting, plumbing fixtures, and other finishes, all in one place. Our experienced designers are available to answer your questions, offer expert guidance, and help you make confident selections that fit your style, lifestyle, and budget.
How does your remodeling process work?
Our proven four-step design-build process guides your project from concept to completion, with a single experienced team managing every detail. We begin by learning about your home, lifestyle, and goals. Next, our designers create custom plans and 3D renderings and guide you through selecting materials and finishes in our Design Center. Once the design and plans are finalized, our skilled craftspeople and project managers oversee construction, keeping your project on schedule and maintaining clear communication every step of the way. Our Four-Step Process:
Imagine: We learn how you live and explore ideas that fit your space and budget
Conceptualize: See your space come to life with 3D designs and a clear scope of work
Collaborate: Make selections and finalize plans with expert guidance at every step
Build: Your dream becomes reality – crafted with care, quality, and respect for your home.
Does RIKB Design Build offer remodeling seminars?
Yes. RIKB Design Build offers complimentary remodeling seminars throughout the year to help homeowners plan with confidence. Led by our award-winning designers, these educational sessions cover remodeling trends, design ideas, budgeting, and what to expect during the remodeling process. Guests can meet our team, explore our 3,000+ square foot Design Center, and gain valuable insights before starting their project.
Does RIKB Design Build remodel historic homes in Rhode Island?
Yes. RIKB Design Build has extensive experience remodeling homes of all ages, including many of the area’s historic and character-filled properties. Our team thoughtfully blends modern functionality with timeless design, preserving the unique architectural details that make older homes special while updating them to better support today’s lifestyles.
Does RIKB Design Build work on coastal homes?
Yes. RIKB Design Build has completed remodeling projects in many of Rhode Island’s coastal communities. Whether you’re updating a year-round residence or a seasonal home, our team understands the importance of choosing durable materials, maximizing natural light and views, and creating spaces that complement the coastal lifestyle.
Planning a Remodeling Project
Should I remodel or move?
Many homeowners love their neighborhood but need a home that better fits their lifestyle. Remodeling can often deliver the updated layout, functionality, and comfort you want while letting you stay where you are. Strategic renovations, such as kitchen remodels, bathroom updates, additions, or reconfigured living spaces, can improve your home’s livability and long-term value. If you enjoy your location but your home no longer meets your needs, remodeling may be a smart investment that helps you love your home again without the expense and disruption of moving.
When is the best time to remodel my home?
The best time to remodel is when your home no longer meets your needs and you’re ready to improve your lifestyle. While many homeowners begin planning in the winter or spring, remodeling projects happen year-round. Starting the planning process early gives you more flexibility in scheduling, design, and material selections, helping your project move more smoothly from concept to completion.
How much should I budget for a home remodel?
The cost of a home remodel depends on the project’s size, scope of work, materials you choose, and the level of customization. Whether you’re remodeling a single room or your entire home, it’s helpful to set an investment range early in the planning process. During your consultation, our team will discuss your goals, priorities, and budget to develop a design that delivers the greatest value for your investment.
How long does a remodeling project take?
Every remodeling project is unique, so the timeline depends on the size, scope, and complexity of the work. Smaller projects may take just a few weeks, while larger renovations or additions typically take longer. During the design phase, we’ll develop a realistic project schedule and keep you informed every step of the way. Because every detail, from design and product selections to construction planning, is finalized before work begins, our design-build process helps minimize delays and keeps your project moving as smoothly as possible.
Why choose a local Rhode Island remodeling company?
Choosing a local remodeling company means working with a team that understands the area’s homes, architecture, building codes, and permitting requirements. With more than 35 years of experience serving homeowners, RIKB Design Build has built strong relationships with trusted local suppliers and craftsmen and has earned a reputation for quality, communication, and exceptional customer service. Our local expertise helps ensure a smoother remodeling experience from start to finish.
Kitchen Remodeling
What adds the most value to a kitchen remodel?
The most valuable kitchen remodels enhance everyday functionality and long-term home value. Features such as an efficient layout, quality cabinetry, durable countertops, a spacious island, ample storage, and layered lighting can make your kitchen more enjoyable and increase its appeal to future buyers. The best investment is one that supports how your family lives while complementing your home’s style.
Is an open-concept kitchen right for my home?
Open-concept kitchens remain among the most popular remodeling choices because they improve flow, increase natural light, and make cooking, entertaining, and time with family easier. However, the best layout depends on your home’s architecture, your lifestyle, and how you use the space. A thoughtful kitchen design should balance openness with storage, functionality, and defined living areas.
What kitchen design trends never go out of style?
Timeless kitchen design prioritizes quality materials and thoughtful planning over short-lived trends. Neutral cabinetry, natural stone or quartz countertops, layered lighting, functional storage, and classic finishes create a kitchen that will look beautiful for years. Choosing durable materials and a layout that supports your daily routine helps ensure your investment stands the test of time.
Are custom cabinets worth the investment?
For many homeowners, custom cabinetry is one of the most worthwhile investments in a kitchen remodel. Custom cabinets maximize storage, improve organization, and are tailored to your space and lifestyle. They also offer greater flexibility in style, finishes, and functionality, helping you create a kitchen that looks beautiful and functions efficiently for years to come.
Bathroom Remodeling
What should I include in a bathroom remodel?
The best bathroom remodels balance style, comfort, and functionality. Popular upgrades include larger walk-in showers, double vanities, improved lighting, additional storage, durable countertops, updated fixtures, and better ventilation. Many homeowners also opt for features such as heated floors, built-in shower niches, and water-efficient fixtures. Prioritizing how you use the space daily will help create a bathroom that is both beautiful and practical.
What is a curbless shower?
A curbless shower is a walk-in shower with no raised threshold between the bathroom floor and the shower area. This seamless design creates a clean, modern look and makes the space feel larger and easier to access. Curbless showers are a popular choice for homeowners planning to age in place because they improve accessibility without sacrificing style. They can also make cleaning easier and add a luxurious, spa-like feel to your bathroom.
What bathroom features add the most value to a home?
Bathrooms that blend timeless design with everyday functionality typically deliver the greatest long-term value. Popular upgrades include walk-in showers, quality vanities, durable countertops, updated lighting, efficient storage, and water-saving fixtures. Choosing classic materials and a thoughtful layout can enhance both your daily routine and your home’s resale appeal.
Design-Build Process
What is the difference between remodeling and renovating?
Although the terms are often used interchangeably, remodeling involves changing a space’s layout, function, or design, while renovating focuses on updating or restoring what’s already there. For example, replacing cabinets and moving walls constitute a remodel, whereas refinishing floors or updating fixtures without changing the layout is a renovation.
Why should I choose a design-build company instead of a traditional contractor?
A design-build company brings design, budgeting, project management, and construction together under one team, creating a more streamlined remodeling experience. Instead of coordinating multiple professionals, you’ll have a single point of contact from concept through completion. This collaborative approach improves communication, helps keep projects on schedule and within budget, and ensures your design vision is carried through every phase of the remodel.
What happens during the design phase?
The design phase is where your vision begins to take shape. You’ll work closely with your designer to develop floor plans, review 3D renderings, select cabinetry, countertops, tile, lighting, fixtures, and other finishes, and establish your project scope and budget. Finalizing these details before construction begins helps minimize surprises and ensures everyone is working toward the same vision.
Why is planning important before a remodeling project begins?
Careful planning is one of the most important steps in a successful remodel. Finalizing the design, selecting materials, setting a realistic budget, and preparing construction plans before work begins help reduce delays, avoid unexpected costs, and create a smoother experience from start to finish. At RIKB, we believe thoughtful planning leads to better results and happier homeowners.
Aging in Place
&
Universal Design
What is aging-in-place remodeling?
Aging-in-place remodeling integrates thoughtful design features that help homeowners stay safe, comfortable, and independent as their needs change over time. Popular upgrades include curbless showers, wider doorways, improved lighting, non-slip flooring, comfort-height fixtures, and first-floor living spaces. These enhancements not only improve accessibility but also create a home that is functional and beautiful for years to come.
What is universal design?
Universal design is an approach to home design that creates spaces that are comfortable, functional, and accessible for people of all ages and abilities. Features such as wider walkways, lever-style door handles, easy-to-reach storage, improved lighting, and barrier-free entries make a home easier to use without sacrificing style. Whether you’re planning for the future or simply want a more livable home today, universal design helps create spaces that work for everyone.

When looking for the best remodeling company to hire for your remodeling project, we urge you to consider several criteria in order to judge the stability and ability of your contractor. Two important factors that remodeling company should have in place are proper licensing and sufficient insurance.
A contractor who is not licensed to do business can easily disappear once a job is finished, leaving you to deal with any problems that arise. Worse, an unlicensed contractor could take your deposit and “fly the coop” before the work is done, leaving you with an unfinished kitchen or bathroom. Licensing demonstrates stability and accountability on the part of the contractor.
RIKB Design Build is a licensed and insured contractor in Rhode Island (Reg#3984), Massachusetts (MA#164199) and Connecticut (CT#HIC.0673137). Rhode Island Kitchen & Bath carries liability insurance up to $2 million for each project, as well as full worker’s compensation insurance for all staff members.
Similarly, a legitimate remodeling company will carry both liability insurance and workers’ compensation insurance. Without this coverage, any accident or injury that occurs in your home may become your liability! Make sure any contractor you are considering has current liability and workers’ compensation coverage. Insist on getting a Certificate of Insurance directly from the company’s insurance carrier.
